title: 2010 AMC 10A Problem 13
statement: Angelina drove at an average rate of \(80\) kph and then stopped \(20\) minutes for gas. After the stop, she drove at an average rate of \(100\) kph. Altogether she drove \(250\) km in a total trip time of \(3\) hours including the stop. Which equation could be used to solve for the time \(t\) in hours that she drove before her stop?

solutions.text:
Before the stop, Angelina drove \(80t\) km.

The stop takes \(\frac{1}{3}\) of an hour, so her total driving time is \(3-\frac13=\frac83\) hours. After the stop, she drives for \(\frac83-t\) hours, covering \(100\left(\frac83-t\right)\) km.

The total distance equation is \(80t+100\left(\frac83-t\right)=250.\)

Thus, A is the correct answer.
hints: Subtract the \(20\)-minute stop from the total time
After the stop, she drives for \(3-\dfrac13-t\) hours
